title: Work experience reflection
lesson_success_checks: Make an honest four-part reflection: what I did, what I learned, what I would do differently, and which expectations I met. Link it to actual work and keep a gap visible. Rate five Week 1 expectations and agree a next step. Staff review six outcomes separately using actual evidence.
source_assessment_summary: Assess actual evidence, with learner reflection/self-assessment separate from the six-outcome teacher review. Staff confirm any accredited mapping.
accreditation: The qualification/accredited unit, mapping confirmed by staff; no named scheme or awarding body.

Six-week term 4 January–12 February; Week 6 is the assessing week. Record actual work-activity date and mode separately from this lesson date. No clock time supplied.

Friday 12 February P1, pair, forty minutes assessing. Structured individual reflection: what I did, learned, would do differently and which expectations I met. Actual invented-workplace work or real placement if it happened. Evidence Sheet has six exact weekly outcomes in a separate teacher-only initially blank tick-and-comment grid; learner five-expectation self-ratings remain separate. No invented experience or prefilled judgements. Further brief follows acceptance only; pause for Downloaded.

routes.Supported: Choose one actual piece of work. Use the four reflection prompts, word bank, model and sentence starts. Plan in your usual way, use an aid or exact scribe, then check the words are your own. Keep gaps visible, rate the five expectations and choose one next step.
routes.Standard: Use actual half-term work or a real placement record if one exists. Complete the four reflection parts with specific examples. Rate the five expectations against your own evidence, explain a gap and agree one next step and help.
routes.Stretch: Compare two actual pieces of evidence or points in your work. Explain what changed, what helped and a limit of your evidence. Use this to justify one future adjustment. Complete the same four reflection parts and five self-ratings; extra writing optional.

business.description: An invented small business prepares simple paper packs for customers. It has a supervisor, a preparer and a checker. It has no name, real employer, location or contact details. This is classroom simulation only.
business.order: Prepare two paper packs. Each pack needs one large card and one paper strip. Put the items beside each other. Check both packs against this order. Tell the checker when they are ready.
business.roles: The preparer arranges the materials. The checker reads the order and checks each pack. Agree roles, then swap after resetting the materials. An adult can take the other role if preferred.
business.limits: Use ready-cut paper only. No scissors, staplers, machines, food, money, customer data, live orders or deliveries. Accuracy, communication and support matter; speed is not assessed.

reflection_sections.label: Which expectations I met
reflection_sections.prompt: Which expectation fits my evidence? Keep any gap visible.

reflection_prompts_short: This shows… The part not seen yet is…
placement_rule: Use the actual half-term workplace activity: the invented classroom simulation, or a real placement if one happened. Record actual activity date, task, role, mode and work reference. No employer, person or place names. Do not invent a placement or completed task. If no activity was completed, mark that and agree a supported follow-up; do not use a model as your own evidence.

teacher_grid_rule: Teacher only: six exact weekly outcomes, each with an initially blank tick cell and comment cell. Tick only when actual evidence supports the outcome. Comment with a work reference, support used and any gap or follow-up. An unticked outcome is not proof of failure. Keep learner self-assessment separate; never prefill the learner ratings.

model.status: Invented example only, not learner evidence.
model.did: A worker read a step and checked one paper pack. The second pack still needed checking.
model.learned: Checking each pack against the order shows what is actually ready.
model.differently: Next time the worker will check or ask for help before calling the whole order complete.
model.expectations: Instructions and quality: one actual check. Asking for help with the next check is a planned next step, not yet observed evidence for Safety and help. Do not claim both packs were complete.

expectations.label: Readiness and reliability
expectations.meaning: Know the agreed start and task. Get agreed materials ready. Tell the supervisor if a delay or support need affects the plan.
expectations.look_for: I checked the task and materials or asked for help to get ready.

expectations.label: Respectful communication
expectations.meaning: Listen or read, use respectful words and check meaning. You can ask for a pause or private help.
expectations.look_for: I listened or read and used a clear question or reply.

expectations.label: Instructions and quality
expectations.meaning: Check the steps. Ask if unsure. Check the finished work against the order before saying it is ready.
expectations.look_for: I checked a step or the finished packs against the order.

expectations.label: Safety and help
expectations.meaning: Keep the work area and access clear. Use only agreed materials. Stop and tell the supervisor if something is unsafe or unclear.
expectations.look_for: I kept the area clear or asked before doing an unclear task.

expectations.label: Teamwork and responsibility
expectations.meaning: Agree roles, share information and report mistakes honestly. Ask for a workable adjustment when needed.
expectations.look_for: I agreed a role, shared a useful update or reported a mistake.

reflection_prompts: I checked the task and materials or asked for help to get ready.
I listened or read and used a clear question or reply.
I checked a step or finished work against the instruction.
I kept the area clear or asked before doing an unclear task.
I agreed a role, shared a useful update or reported a mistake.
rating_states: I did this with a prompt
worked_examples_status: The workplace and balanced reflection model are invented and declared. Model: one checked pack and a second still needing checking, not a claim that a learner completed both. Record actual date, mode, task, role, work reference, learning and any gap honestly. No real employer, person, product or place named.
private_help_route: Trusted adult or school help route. Point to HELP, write or ask privately. If one adult is busy, use the route to another. Pass, pause and supported return available. No personal customer, employment or family account requested.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Evidence Sheet pages 2–3: ten blank typed reflection fields and separate five-expectation review/next steps. Page 4 teacher-only six-outcome grid has initially blank tick/comment cells and four closing fields. Book/voice/aid/typing/exact scribe valid; read back/correct. Use actual work; keep gaps visible.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: one actual item, four short prompts, visible example and reduced writing. Communication and Interaction: rehearsal, wait time, usual aid and exact scribe/readback. SEMH: predictable private review, pass and pause/return; no personality grade. Sensory and Physical: accessible table, large print and seated response. EAL: plan in any language. 1 Point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 scaffold/choice; 5 model first step only then return task.
worked_example_and_fade: Only one pack was checked in the invented example. Instructions and quality has one stated check; help-seeking is a proposed next step, not a performed action. Keep actual evidence, frames and normal aids visible. Fade answer cues only; a normal aid is access. Do not require a perfect story, full output or invented weakness.

main_hinge.claim: Keep the unchecked part visible and choose an evidence-linked improvement rather than claim the whole task is complete.

parallel_hinge.claim: Use actual work with its mode, date and reference, or state a gap, rather than copy a model as personal evidence.

assessment: Keep the four reflection parts, an actual evidence clue, a visible gap and next step/reply. Learner ratings remain: I did this; I did this with a prompt; I need another try; Not seen today. Staff never prefill these. Teacher only: six exact weekly outcomes, each with an initially blank tick cell and comment cell. Tick only when actual evidence supports the outcome. Comment with a work reference, support used and any gap or follow-up. An unticked outcome is not proof of failure. Keep learner self-assessment separate; never prefill the learner ratings. Judge links between claims, work and future adjustment; no personality, reading-fluency, pace or attendance inference.

evidence.description: Individual actual work reference/date/mode, four-part reflection, five learner expectation ratings and next step/reply; separate teacher-only six-outcome evidence review with honest gaps.

where_this_leads: This helps me explain what I have learned from work, recognise support that helped and plan a useful adjustment for a next task.
colour_blind_safe: Written section labels, numbered prompts and words carry meaning; no colour-only states.

asset.description: Unchanged generated workroom bank from accepted Week 5, originally Week 2. Only controlled view D used, in native crops; generic invented workers/workplace. It is context, not proof of learner participation.
